title: HSBC Layoffs: Bank to slash half of UK wealth management and specialist roles; AI push costs recent job cuts
source_used: The Independent, relaying the Financial Times
key_facts: HSBC is in a consultation period over proposed changes to its UK wealth management business.
About half of the division's management and specialist roles are expected to go, and financial advisers could be cut by up to around 70%, the FT reported, citing an anonymous source.
The FT source called the cuts "deep, wide and brutal".
Affected staff are expected to leave at the end of October.
CEO Georges Elhedery backs AI tools; relationship managers have been given AI to serve clients faster.
HSBC UK said it is evolving to deliver more digitally enabled products.
quote_evidence: Around half of the wealth division’s management and specialist roles are expected to be cut, while its financial advisers will be reduced by up to around 70%, the Financial Times (FT) reported, citing an anonymous source familiar with the plans.
The FT cited one source describing the cuts as “deep, wide and brutal” and that almost entire teams would be made redundant.
why_it_matters_hint: A major bank is reported to be replacing much of its UK wealth staff with digital and AI services.
